title: Skip bin of rubble on a flatbed (rear)
blurb: A rusty yellow skip bin full of rubble on a flatbed, shot from a following car; a single pale-blue strap runs diagonally over it.
photo_credit: Photo: Fabian Horst, CC BY-SA 4.0 via Wikimedia Commons. QA sweep development run, Oct 26, 2026.

calibration.axis: x (front at bed_min_x, rear at bed_max_x)
calibration.method: pixels-per-inch = trailer_bed mask bitmap tight extent along x (3015 px) / user-supplied bed length (20.0 ft = 240 in)

measurements.name: rear_overhang
measurements.method: rearmost cargo extent (mask bitmap tight edge, else bbox) minus the bed rear edge, scaled by the calibration; rear = image-right end of the bed extent
measurements.reason: no cargo detections, so there is no load extent to compare with the bed

measurements.name: load_centroid_vs_axle
measurements.method: bitmap-weighted centroid of all cargo masks along the bed axis vs the axle estimate position (midpoint of axle centres when several), scaled by the calibration
measurements.reason: no cargo detections, so there is no load centroid to place

measurements.name: tarp_coverage
measurements.method: tarp/canvas mask area overlapping the cargo area, as a percentage of the cargo area (bitmap union on the image canvas)
measurements.reason: load type is 'general', not loose material; the tarp check only applies to loose loads

measurements.name: tiedown_coverage_gaps
measurements.method: tie-down anchor positions mapped onto the bed axis (anchor centre x in bed coordinates); spans between neighbouring anchors and the bed ends, scaled by the calibration
measurements.reason: no tie-down detections in this detection set: tie-downs are counted from anchor close-up photos plus tap-to-correct, and close-up coordinates live in the close-up photo's own image space, so they cannot be placed on this photo's bed axis

notes: load_centroid_vs_axle is a visual estimate of where the load's bulk sits; it is not a weight measurement

verdicts.finding: Forward blocking cannot be judged: no cargo detections in the side photo, so the load's front edge cannot be placed against the front of the bed.
verdicts.confidence_basis: calibration present but no cargo detections

verdicts.finding: This load needs 3 tie-down(s) for its length (12 ft), but no tie-downs could be counted: tie-downs are counted from anchor close-up photos plus any you mark by tapping them on the photo, and neither was supplied. Full-frame photos cannot count straps reliably (they are too thin to read at that distance).
verdicts.confidence_basis: no close-up detection set and no user tie-down marks supplied

verdicts.cfr_citation: 49 CFR Part 393, Subpart I (overhang; lights and plate visibility)
verdicts.finding: Overhang: could not be measured (no cargo detections, so there is no load extent to compare with the bed). Lights and plate: the rear photo read reports both visible and unobscured.
verdicts.confidence_basis: lights/plate from the dual-model cross-check rear read (Muse Spark); SAM has no equivalent signal
verdicts.citation: 49 CFR Part 393, Subpart I (overhang; lights and plate visibility)

verdicts.cfr_citation: 49 CFR 393.100 (load placement; visual estimate only here)
verdicts.finding: Weight placement cannot be called: no cargo detections, so there is no load centroid to place. Placement is a visual estimate only in any case - a photo shows where the bulk sits, never how heavy it is.
verdicts.confidence_basis: visual estimate only; no usable centroid measurement
verdicts.citation: 49 CFR 393.100 (load placement; visual estimate only here)

verdicts.finding: Edge protection cannot be judged from the evidence supplied: it needs a close-up of each strap where it crosses an edge, read for protectors. Take an anchor close-up per tie-down and run the cross-check.
verdicts.confidence_basis: no close-up cross-check evidence about straps over edges

verdicts.finding: Tie-down strength cannot be checked from the photo: a photo cannot verify working load limit ratings or load weight, and this check needs both numbers. Missing: no tie-down working load limit ratings were supplied; no load weight was supplied. Supply the load weight and each tie-down's rating and this check runs on those numbers.
verdicts.confidence_basis: not computable: no tie-down working load limit ratings were supplied; no load weight was supplied

report.headline: Load could not be judged from photos given
report.body:
Forward blocking could not be judged. No cargo was seen in the side photo so the front edge cannot be placed. Supply a side photo showing the cargo against the front of the bed.
This 12 ft load needs 3 tie-downs but none could be counted. Supply anchor close-up photos or mark tie-downs by tapping them on the photo.
Overhang could not be measured with no cargo detections to compare with the bed. The rear photo read reports lights and plate visible and unobscured.
Weight placement could not be called with no centroid to place. It needs cargo visible, and it is a visual estimate only.
Edge protection could not be judged. It needs a close-up of each strap where it crosses an edge. Take an anchor close-up per tie-down.
Tie-down strength could not be checked. It needs working load limit ratings and load weight.
A photo cannot verify strap tension, tie-down ratings, or load weight.
